messages.content: You are an operations assistant for Northstar Manufacturing's procurement process. Answer questions about procurement policy, SLA targets, escalation procedures, vendor onboarding, and contract renewal using only the policy information you know. What are the approval requirements?

According to Procurement Policy, Section 4.1 Standard Approval: 4.1 Standard Approval
Purchase Orders up to $10,000 require single-level approval from the requesting department's
budget owner.

When is an SLA breach reported?

According to SLA Policy, Section 4. Breach Reporting: 4. Breach Reporting
Any case whose cycle time exceeds its category's target is reported as an SLA breach in the
weekly operations management report. A single breach does not trigger automatic escalation --
see the Escalation Procedure for when escalation is required.

meta.citation: SLA Policy, Section 4. Breach Reporting

What are the inspection requirements?

According to Quality Control Procedure, Section 2. Incoming Inspection: 2. Incoming Inspection
Every delivery is inspected against the Purchase Order specification before the receiving dock
marks it complete. Inspection is sampling-based: a 10% sample for standard orders, 100% inspection
for any order from a supplier under Manual Credit Review (Procurement Policy Section 5) or any
supplier still in the Vendor Onboarding trial-order stage.

meta.citation: Quality Control Procedure, Section 2. Incoming Inspection

What is the dollar threshold below which a buyer may self-approve a purchase without Procurement review?

According to Procurement Policy, Section 3. Purchase Requisition: 3. Purchase Requisition

be self-approved by the requesting department manager. Requisitions above $500 require Procurement
review before a Purchase Order is issued.

What is the SLA target for Consignment orders?

According to Inventory Management Policy, Section 2. Reorder Point Calculation: 2. Reorder Point Calculation
Each SKU's reorder point is set at (average daily usage x supplier lead time) + safety stock.
Lead time is the supplier's category-level SLA target from the SLA Policy, not the supplier's
historical average -- using the SLA target keeps reorder points aligned with what Procurement is
contractually expecting, not what has merely been observed.

meta.citation: Inventory Management Policy, Section 2. Reorder Point Calculation

According to Procurement Policy, Section 7. Service Level Targets: 7. Service Level Targets
Standard Purchase Orders are targeted for approval within 5 business days of requisition
submission. High-value orders requiring secondary approval are targeted for 10 business days.
These targets are business goals, not contractual guarantees to suppliers.

A case has breached its SLA target by 6 business days. What action does policy require?

According to Procurement Escalation Procedure, Section 1. When to Escalate: 1. When to Escalate
A case should be escalated to Operations leadership when any of the following apply:
- The case has breached its SLA target (see SLA Policy) by more than 5 business days
- The case has undergone more than 2 rounds of PO Change Approval
- A supplier is unresponsive for more than 3 business days during Manual Credit Review

An emergency purchase is made from a supplier with zero prior completed orders. In what order must the required processes be completed?

According to Exception Handling Procedure, Section 2. Emergency Purchases: 2. Emergency Purchases
An emergency purchase (production-stopping shortage) may bypass standard requisition approval
with verbal authorization from a department manager, but must have a retroactive Purchase
Requisition filed within 2 business days. Emergency purchases are still subject to Manual Credit
Review if the supplier meets the criteria in Procurement Policy Section 5.

meta.citation: Exception Handling Procedure, Section 2. Emergency Purchases

If a data-entry error in a record is corrected, is the original erroneous entry deleted?

According to Exception Handling Procedure, Section 4. Data Corrections: 4. Data Corrections
If a case's recorded activity sequence contains an obvious data-entry error (e.g. a duplicate
Approval event from a system glitch, not an actual second approval), Operations may flag it for
manual correction in the source system. This procedure does not authorize retroactively changing
what actually happened -- only correcting erroneous records of what happened.

meta.citation: Exception Handling Procedure, Section 4. Data Corrections

A supplier dispute is raised on a case already 3 days past its SLA target. Does the dispute hold pause the SLA clock from that point forward?

According to Quality Control Procedure, Section 4. Rework vs. Return: 4. Rework vs. Return
A Minor or Major defect may be reworked on-site if the supplier agrees to cover rework cost and
the rework can complete within 3 business days without affecting the case's SLA target. Otherwise
the delivery is returned and treated as a Supplier Dispute under Exception Handling Procedure
Section 3 -- the SLA hold provisions there apply identically to a quality-driven dispute.

What shields a case from being marked a breach when the vendor is contesting the order terms?

According to Exception Handling Procedure, Section 3. Supplier Disputes: 3. Supplier Disputes
If a supplier disputes an order's terms after PO release, the case is held (not cancelled) pending
resolution, and does not count toward SLA breach metrics during the hold period -- this is the one
documented exception to the SLA Policy's Section 3 rule that all process time counts.

What triggers a formal review of a supplier's creditworthiness when a new purchase order is submitted?

According to Procurement Policy, Section 5. Manual Credit Review: 5. Manual Credit Review
Orders from a new supplier (fewer than 3 prior completed orders) or from a supplier with a
below-threshold vendor risk score automatically route to Manual Credit Review regardless of order
value. Manual Credit Review is performed by the Vendor Risk team and is not bound by the standard
approval SLA in Section 7.

meta.citation: Procurement Policy, Section 5. Manual Credit Review

Does the escalation process allow the Operations Director to waive the secondary approval requirement for high-value orders?

According to Procurement Policy, Section 4.2 Secondary Approval: 4.2 Secondary Approval
Purchase Orders above $10,000, or any order flagged as high-risk by the credit/vendor risk
screening, require a second approval from Procurement leadership before the order is released to
the supplier. This is the primary source of processing delay for high-value orders -- see the
companion operations-performance project's SLA-breach driver analysis.

What happens to a delivery that contains a Critical defect?

According to Quality Control Procedure, Section 3. Defect Classification: 3. Defect Classification
Defects are classified Minor, Major, or Critical. A Critical defect (safety risk or complete
non-conformance to spec) triggers an automatic hold on the entire delivery and a Safety Incident
Report if the defect could have reached the production line undetected -- see Safety Incident
Reporting Procedure Section 2.
